report_name: New CSS Attacks Bypass Webmail Defenses to Steal Credentials, Tokens

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The attack is delivered via a maliciously crafted HTML email which the victim must open in a vulnerable webmail client.

attack_patterns.name: Web Portal Capture
attack_patterns.description: CSS abuse techniques are used to create a fake password input field that overlays the legitimate webmail UI to steal user credentials, as demonstrated in a proof-of-concept against Microsoft Outlook.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: A proof-of-concept attack demonstrated how a malicious email could manipulate the UI of a Gmail integration with Anthropic's Claude AI to trick a user into leaking a Slack token.

attack_patterns.name: Content Injection
attack_patterns.description: Malicious CSS is injected into an HTML email to manipulate the presentation of the webmail client's UI, causing content to be rendered outside its intended sandboxed boundaries.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution
attack_patterns.description: The attack requires a user to open the maliciously crafted HTML email within a vulnerable webmail client to trigger the exploit.

vulnerabilities.name: CSS Injection in Webmail Clients
vulnerabilities.description: A class of vulnerabilities where CSS properties in an HTML email are abused to escape the security sandbox and overlay the trusted webmail UI, enabling credential theft, token exfiltration, and UI redressing.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Vendor of Outlook, a webmail service demonstrated to be vulnerable to the CSS injection attacks.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Vendor of Gmail, a webmail service demonstrated to be vulnerable to the CSS injection attacks.

identities.description: A webmail service identified as being affected by the CSS injection vulnerability.
